source.title: Common Neural Network for Different Functions: An Investigation of Proactive and Reactive Inhibition

confidence_rationale: Direct anchor for the claim: whole-brain fMRI plus Bayesian model selection over 70+13 DCMs isolates a 'longer' DLPFC->caudate->IFG->SMA->STN->M1 pathway whose caudate->IFG link is modulated ONLY under proactive inhibition, versus a 'shorter' IFG->SMA->STN->M1 hyperdirect pathway carrying reactive inhibition. This is exactly the two-pathway dissociation MECH-141 asserts. Confidence held below 0.85 because the paper's own framing is a COMMON network (shared IFG-SMA-STN-M1 core), so it evidences dissociation at the modulatory-connectivity level rather than fully segregated anatomy, and DCM is a model-comparison inference, not a direct latency measurement of the two timescales.
failure_signatures: The two pathways share the IFG-SMA-STN-M1 core; the dissociation is in which effective connections are modulated, not in fully non-overlapping anatomy. A substrate that collapsed the shared core while preserving the distinct front-end modulation would still satisfy this paper's evidence, so the paper does not on its own falsify a partially-collapsed arbitration signal.
Timescale segregation (seconds vs milliseconds) is inferred from the pathway lengths and task structure, not measured directly here; DCM reports connection strengths, not conduction latencies.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Proactive and reactive inhibition are subserved by fronto-basal-ganglia pathways of different length within a common network: a longer DLPFC-caudate-IFG-SMA-STN-M1 pathway (caudate->IFG modulated only under proactive inhibition) and a shorter IFG-SMA-STN-M1 hyperdirect pathway for reactive inhibition, providing causal evidence for indirect vs hyperdirect roles.
mapping.ree_translation: The slow proactive pathway (DLPFC->caudate->IFG) maps onto E3 pre-commit eligibility assessment that pre-sets gate bias from prior planning; the fast hyperdirect (IFG->SMA->STN) pathway maps onto a rapid post-commitment interrupt at the cancel-window (MECH-138) but at a shorter timescale. MECH-141 requires both to be present and NOT collapsible into a single arbitration signal.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper demonstrates two dissociable MODULATORY pathways within a shared node set, not two anatomically segregated circuits. It therefore supports 'two dissociable pathways' strongly and 'cannot be collapsed' only at the connectivity/timescale level; a REE substrate could in principle share compute for the common core. The timescale separation itself is inferred, not directly timed.
mapping.source_context: Human fMRI, stop-signal task, healthy adults; effective connectivity via Dynamic Causal Modeling with Bayesian model selection.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality moderate: peer-reviewed fMRI+DCM but a specialist journal with a modest sample and model-based (not latency-based) inference. Mapping fidelity high -- the paper's own proactive/reactive x long/short pathway structure is a near-literal instantiation of MECH-141. Transfer risk moderate: human data (good), but task-to-REE-arbitration transfer requires accepting the E3-eligibility mapping.
